Banca Divinef-Front Page April 4, 1990
Committee hears smoking discussion
A County Council committee meeting was held Tuesday night before the regularly scheduled council meeting to discuss smoking policy for county buildings.
A- group of about 20 county workers was on hand to speak before the council on the matter of smoking in public buildings.
The council took the suggestions by the public under advisement and, ' according to committee member Dr. Julius Earle, the committee will present its findings to the council as early as their next meeting, April 17. A final decision will not be made at that time and he asked for more public comment.
Sheriff's deputy Steve Pruitt said that although he was a non-smoker Sheriff Earl Holcomb said he he sympathized with those who would like to see designated areas smoke, "They are addicted just like an alcoholic or drug addict," he said; " 'smoker, and we're fooling ourselves " "but they make us suffer like a drunk driver who kills on the highways or a heroin addict spreads AIDS with his dirty needles." There was a sustained applause at his remarks.
Pruitt also discussed, insurance
benefits and civil liabilities in cases of non-smokers bringing suit against smokers.
Sally Smith, records clerk at the courthouse, said she was afraid of fire. "There are records that go back to 1840 and cannot be replaced." she said. Smith held up a paper that had been retrieved from a wastebasket in the records room that had a cigarette hole burned through it.
Fire Marshall Dewiu Mize said that smoking is a fire hazard. "Cigarettes have caused tremendous fires in. buildings in Oconee County," he said, "I want to go on record as saying we need to work out some system for controlling smoking in public buildings."
